props.gloss_en: R' Chiyya (statement I): total denial met by witnesses attesting fifty -- he pays the fifty and swears on the remainder
R' Chiyya (statement II): 'you have only fifty -- and here it is' still obligates the oath of partial admission
the reason: tendering the admitted part is still an admission to part of the claim
two grasping a garment, each claiming all: each swears he owns no less than half, and they divide it
Rabba: the presumption -- a person does not brazenly deny outright before his creditor
the partial admitter is really dodging until he can pay, so the Torah lays an oath on him to force full admission -- a psychology absent when witnesses attest, hence the need for the kal vachomer
a litigant's own admission is as a hundred witnesses (for money, though not for a fine)
two witnesses say 'you ate forbidden fat' and he denies it: R' Meir obligates the korban
the Chachamim exempt him from the korban
Rav Idi bar Avin citing Rav Chisda: one who denies a loan remains kosher for testimony (he may be dodging); a deposit-denier is disqualified
Rav Sheshet: with 'here it is' the admitted coins are as already collected, so no oath of partial admission arises
defense (c, final): the mishna's oath is rabbinic, so it does not bear on Sumchos's Torah-level rule
the rejoinder: the Sages model their oaths on Torah oaths, so a rabbinic oath in the mishnah presupposes that הילך is liable by Torah law
